audio_caption: The audio starts with a male speaker asking, "Is it too late to start wrestling?". He acknowledges that it's a common question he gets asked. He asks the audience to like and subscribe, explaining that it helps promote his content. He explains that likes and subscriptions help his videos get promoted. He explains that he's doing this for free and sharing information with the audience. He mentions potential future plans like starting a wrestling gym, recording content, and fighting in MMA, noting that it's taking too long. He asks people to smash the like button and subscribe button.

The clip starts with one male speaker, who starts his monologue by saying that they are "getting right into it" and moves onto the question of, "is it too late to start wrestling?". He emphasizes the best time to learn wrestling is in school, at any age. He moves onto the availability of wrestling and it being easier to start when you're younger. He says that being a senior is "no excuse" to not join a wrestling team, and that there will be beginners at every stage in school, from first to eighth grade. To summarize, he encourages joining as the best time to start is right now. The clip ends on a question.

The clip features a single male speaker, conversational and encouraging, discussing learning wrestling in school and how starting earlier reduces effort needed to excel. The tone is positive as he details how dedicated practice, even with less intensity, leads to success. There is a background hum throughout.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker describing the challenges of starting wrestling later in life, explaining that the amount one needs to improve increases with each day not spent wrestling because their competition is improving while they remain stagnant. He encourages listeners by saying that it doesn't mean working to the top is impossible. The tone is conversational and encouraging.

The audio clip begins with a single male speaker who describes starting wrestling in high school. His tone is motivational as he stresses the importance of hard work and dedication to the sport, saying it is "very possible" to be successful. He advises wrestling in the off-season and doing everything you need to do, noting that he makes videos on how to be a better wrestler and how starting earlier is better.

The clip starts with a male speaker expressing a problem, stating "Now the problem is, once you get out of high school..." Continuing in a conversational tone, he explains how beginner classes, practices teaching fundamentals like single leg, double leg, and level changes, become scarce. He notes that such instruction thins "very, very, very heavily," especially between college wrestling and wrestling club. He mentions the context of wrestling in club, for college.

The audio clip features a single male speaker advising someone to join a school wrestling team immediately if possible. He conveys that new wrestlers will face a steep learning curve, being "eaten up and chewed at" and potentially not achieving a takedown until later in their training. He attributes this to the higher level of competition found in college. The speaker's tone is motivational and encouraging.

The clip features a single male speaker with a somewhat serious, informative tone, discussing wrestling and MMA gyms, arguing the latter is the "weakest form of wrestling training". He discusses joining an MMA gym as a last resort, highlighting its downsides and differences compared to school wrestling teams. His tone expresses frustration, stating, "This sucks".

The audio clip begins with a speaker emphasizing "legit competition" and people trying to take one's spot, highlighting the irreplaceable nature of the situation. The speaker has a straightforward tone. This is followed by silence.

The audio clip begins with one male speaker providing an encouraging message, stating "it's never too late to start" and emphasizing the importance of starting early to reach the top level of wrestling. The speaker maintains a motivational tone, explaining that this advice will benefit the listener in every aspect of their life.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker encouraging the listener to "just try it," referring to wrestling, explaining its benefits across life aspects like work ethic and decision-making. The tone is motivational, emphasizing the unique training wrestling offers, unavailable in typical schooling environments. Then it ends there.

The audio clip features one male speaker discussing the challenges of joining college wrestling versus high school, citing a steeper learning curve and more competitive environment. He suggests starting younger, emphasizing the benefits wrestling can bring to other aspects of life and the addictiveness of the sport. His tone is informative and encouraging. The background is silent, but abruptly transitions to music. The music style is a simple song with a light, uplifting tone.

The audio clip begins with speech from a single male speaker. He encourages viewers to like and subscribe, mentioning posting content daily and promising to see them again, concluding with "peace." The clip then ends abruptly.
